**Find the Right Storage Features for Your Needs**


If you’re comparing storage options, it’s easy to focus exclusively on finding a convenient location and the right unit size. But to get the most out of your self-storage experience, it’s also worth considering all the other on-site amenities and facility features that can make storing and accessing your belongings much easier.


In this guide, we’ll take a closer look at some of the top features available at most CubeSmart storage facilities, including property and facility amenities and unit-level features. That way, you can make an informed decision about the best storage option for you, whether you’re moving, decluttering, running a business, or just looking for a place to store your seasonal items.


## Top Features of CubeSmart Storage Facilities


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/man-in-black-shirt-delivering-the-boxes-7362919/)


All[CubeSmart services](https://www.cubesmart.com/cubesmart-services) and features are designed to create a convenient and reliable storage experience. Here’s a closer look at some of the features you may find at your local CubeSmart location.


### Property and Facility Features


The first thing you might notice when visiting a CubeSmart location is how easy the property is to navigate. These features are designed to create a smooth storage experience from the moment you arrive.


#### Electronic Gate Access


Many CubeSmart locations offer electronic gate access with your own personal access code. At some facilities, you can also use remote-controlled access for entry gates, loading dock doors, or even your storage unit door.*


#### Routine Facility Inspections


All CubeSmart storage facilities also receive routine facility inspections to ensure our renters have a pleasant and consistent experience every time they visit. These regular inspections help ensure that the common areas, buildings, and grounds remain well-maintained.


#### On-Site Resident Managers


Many CubeSmart storage facilities also have on-site resident managers available to provide customer support and answer any questions that may come up about renting a unit or navigating the facility.


### Unit-Level Features


The features inside your storage unit can have just as much impact on your overall experience as the property itself. Here are some common unit-level features available at CubeSmart storage facilities.


#### Climate-Controlled Storage


Climate-controlled storage is one of the more popular features available at many CubeSmart storage facilities. These units reasonably maintain a temperature range, which means they’re a great choice for items like electronics, wooden furniture, and other[things that need climate-controlled storage](https://www.cubesmart.com/blog/your-space/organization/10-surprising-things-that-need-climate-controlled-storage/) . If you’re storing temperature-sensitive items, climate-controlled storage is worth considering.**


#### Individual Unit Lighting and Electricity


Some CubeSmart storage facilities offer individual unit lighting and electricity. This feature can be especially useful if you’re using self-storage for your business and need to regularly sift through inventory, equipment, or supplies within your unit.


#### Storage Unit Locks


While CubeSmart provides a secure place to store your items, you’re responsible for bringing and maintaining your own storage unit locks. Not all locks are the same for a storage unit, so it’s worth choosing one that’s built to last.


Here are some of the most common storage unit lock options:


- **Disc Locks:** Disc locks have a rounded design that leaves very little of the shackle exposed, which makes them more difficult to cut. They’re often considered the best storage unit locks, since they’re compact, resistant to bolt cutters and lock picking, and fit most storage unit doors.
- **Padlocks:** Traditional padlocks are easy to find, easy to use, and come in a range of sizes. If you go with a padlock, though, you’ll want to choose a heavy-duty model with a hardened steel shackle that’s harder to break.
- **Cylinder Locks:** Cylinder locks fit directly into your storage door’s built-in locking mechanism as they’re only compatible with specific units.
- **Smart Locks:** Some storage unit locks connect to a mobile app, which can let you unlock your unit with your phone, share temporary access, or view activity.


## FAQs: Storage Facility Features


Free image via[Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/silver-and-black-combination-lock-J4eTN9GqhzI)


### What Features Should I Look for in a Storage Facility?


When comparing storage facilities, it helps to look beyond just the unit size and price. Features that make your experience more convenient can make a big difference.


Some of the most useful amenities customers look for include electronic gate access, climate-controlled units, on-site managers, and video recording.** Depending on what you’re storing, you may also want features like drive-up access or extras like individual-unit shelving, lighting, and electrical outlets.*


### What Type of Lock Is Best for a Storage Unit?


Most people consider disc locks to be the best locks for a storage unit. They’re the industry standard for a reason: they’re compact, resistant to bolt cutters and lock picking, and work with most storage unit doors. If you’d rather not keep track of keys, a keyless lock can also be a great option for added convenience. Just keep in mind that any storage unit lock you plan to use must be shown to and approved by the facility’s general manager before it can be placed on your unit.


### What Features Make Moving Into a Storage Unit Faster and Easier?


Drive-up access is one of the most convenient features you can look for with self-storage.* With drive-up access, you can park right outside your unit to load and unload quickly and easily, instead of carrying your belongings across a parking lot or through long hallways.* This is especially helpful if you’re moving heavy or bulky items like furniture, appliances, or workout equipment.**


### What Features Help Keep Stored Items in Good Condition Year-Round?


If you’re concerned about how seasonal temperature changes could affect the more sensitive items you want to store, like wooden furniture or electronics, climate-controlled storage can help keep them in a reasonably maintained temperature range year-round.**


Climate-controlled storage isn’t always necessary, but it’s worth considering, particularly when you live somewhere very hot or very cold. For example, people[storing a motorcycle](https://www.cubesmart.com/blog/storage/how-to-store-a-motorcycle-for-winter/) may choose indoor storage if their city regularly experiences extreme summer heat or severe winter snowstorms.**
